newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec same-store sales up 0.3 pct - Telecheck.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec same-store sales up 0.3 pct - Telecheck.

text.p: U.S. December same-store retail sales rose 0.3 percent from a year earlier, Telecheck Services said Tuesday.
Same-store retail sales rose 2.4 percent for the entire holiday period ended December 24, the check-acceptance company said. Telecheck had projected an increase of 2.0-4.0 percent.
Data are based on a year-over-year, same-store comparison of the dollar volume of authorized checks written by consumers at more than 27,000 of TeleCheck's 160,000 subscribing locations.
Telecheck is a subsidiary of First Data Corp.

"The holiday season overall was a disappointment to many of America's retailers. Certainly, the five fewer holiday shopping days this season (than in 1995) affected retail sales, along with the value-conscious shopping habits that consumers have exhibited over the past several years," said Dr. William Ford, TeleCheck's senior economic adviser.
He said December sales were hurt by the fact there was one less Saturday this year than last, and by severe winter storms that hit the Northwest immediately after Christmas.

For the holiday period, retail sales rose 4.7 percent in the Mid-Atlantic region, 3.1 percent in the Southwest, 2.9 percent in the Northeast, 1.8 percent in the West, and 1.3 percent in both the Southeast and Midwest.
TeleCheck's figures are not adjusted for inflation.
